dedupe_keys.name: vitoria gasteiz green urban infrastructure strategy

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Green Urban Infrastructure Strategy launched by the City Council of Vitoria-Gasteiz, Spain, in 2012 to regenerate degraded areas through eco-design, enhance urban biodiversity, connect urban and peri-urban green spaces around the city's Green Belt, and raise adaptive capacity to heatwaves and floods. Projections cited include spring rainfall falling 10 to 30 percent by 2100, up to 30 percent more extreme rainfall events and warmer winters and summers. Interventions include the eco-design renovation of Gasteiz Avenue completed in 2014 and the green facade of the Europa Congress Palace (about 10 million euros together), the Green Ring works (about 2 million euros over four years) and the naturalisation of green spaces and vacant plots in the Lakuabizkarra neighbourhood in 2015-2016 (415,000 euros). Coverage is the city and its peri-urban ring. The page, published in 2018 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the municipal strategy documents. Caveats: adaptation benefits such as heat island reduction are described qualitatively, not measured, and the strategy mixes many objectives. It illustrates city-scale green and blue infrastructure planning for climate adaptation against heat and flood hazards; related records are the Copernicus Urban Atlas and the Stuttgart ventilation corridors case study.
name: Vitoria-Gasteiz Green Urban Infrastructure Strategy
outcomes: Eco-designed Gasteiz Avenue, a green facade on the Europa Congress Palace, Green Ring works and naturalised plots in Lakuabizkarra were delivered, with citizen involvement cited as a success factor.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the Center for Environmental Studies of Vitoria-Gasteiz City Council
